\section{Known-Truth Validation Results}
Hard gates are enforced. The low-dimensional action-dependent DGP is a sanity check; the high-dimensional action-dependent DGP is the main NNES validation because it exercises the larger state and reward-feature setting where the neural estimator is meant to matter.

\subsection{Validation Design Context}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{low-dimensional action-dependent DGP.} A compact finite-state DDC benchmark with action-specific rewards, known transitions, known reward, value, policy, and Q-function truth, and Type A/B/C counterfactual oracles.
\item \textbf{high-dimensional action-dependent DGP.} A harder encoded-state and richer reward-feature stress cell using the same known-truth reward, value, policy, Q-function, and Type A/B/C counterfactual objects to test scaling beyond the compact tabular case.
\end{itemize}

Both cells use 2,000 simulated individuals, 80 periods per individual, known transitions, three actions, homogeneous rewards, and the shared Type A/B/C counterfactual oracles. The high-dimensional cell is the primary stress test; the low-dimensional cell checks that the same implementation still behaves correctly in the easy benchmark.

The high-dimensional DGP passes the pre-estimation checks before NNES is fit: feature rank is 32/32, the reward-feature condition number is 1.377, all 81 states are observed, and state-action coverage is 0.959.
